notes: Corpo-Cards, the in-game trading card game (SERVER + DB + CLIENT: pm2 restart AND hard-refresh). Everything card-related now lives in one top-level Corpo-Cards tab (formerly Arena) with views Play, Decks, Collection, Rules, Card Packs, and Ƒbay; the Store tab no longer has a card subtab (it is back to Titles/Inventory/Ƒbay/Slots). Buy packs (Card Packs), open them, build decks from cards you own (9 slots; validateDeck enforced client and server: 20 cards, one faction + neutrals, max 2 per card / 1 for legendaries), and play PvE matches vs the AI (rules engine runs client-side). Seven buildable factions, each with a starter deck so an empty collection can still play; shiny is an orthogonal cosmetic variant. Pack buying is server-authoritative: the server owns the price, the rarity and shiny rolls, the cash debit, and the writes; cards are granted before cash is debited so a DB fault can never take money or leave phantom cards. New additive tables tcg_collection and tcg_decks (plus tcg_card_market); new server/tcg/packs.js and server/tcg/tcg-db.js; db.js calls initTcg(db). Five packs: Starter F25,000, Standard F150,000 (>=1 Rare), Premium F750,000 (>=1 Epic), Guild Crate F500,000 (Dwarves-only), The Vault F5,000,000 (guaranteed Legendary). Ƒbay card market: list any owned card at any price for Social Credits and browse/buy/cancel; a buy moves the card and cash in ONE SQLite transaction with relative cash updates, which is dupe/refund-proof under the fresh-per-message actor model. Listing a card removes it from play: a deck that needs a listed card is unplayable until you unlist it (the copy returns) or sell it (swap the card out). Rules tab documents the full ruleset in the game's own terms. Casino: blackjack and poker now render pixel-art cards from a shared sprite sheet (casino-cards.js + assets/cards/poker-deck.png) with a text-glyph fallback. Tab strip is now a single horizontal scroll-strip instead of wrapping to a second row. Matches are PvE; PvP / a server-authoritative match loop is not yet built. Em dashes are purged from player-visible card-game strings.
